sanskrit: śrutvā tu pitaraṃ vṛttaṃ bhrātaru ca vivāsitau bharato duḥkhasaṃtapta idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having heard of his father's death and his two brothers exiled, Bharata, scorched with grief, spoke these words:

sanskrit: kiṃ nuṇkāryaṃ hatasyeha mama rājyena śocataḥ vihīnasyātha pitrā ca bhrātrā pitṛsamena ca
english: "What use is a kingdom to me, a ruined and grieving man, bereft of my father and of a brother who is equal to a father?"

sanskrit: duḥkhe me duḥkham akaror vraṇe kṣāram ivādadhāḥ rājānaṃ pretabhāvasthaṃ kṛtvā rāmaṃ ca tāpasaṃ
english: "You have heaped sorrow upon my sorrow, pouring salt into a wound — having reduced the king to the state of a departed spirit and Rāma to an ascetic."

sanskrit: kulasya tvam abhāvāya kālarātrir ivāgatā aṅgāram upagūhya sma pitā me nāvabuddhavān
english: "You have come like the night of doom for the destruction of our lineage; my father, embracing a live coal, did not perceive the danger."

sanskrit: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca putraśokābhipīḍite duṣkaraṃ yadi jīvetāṃ prāpya tvāṃ jananīṃ mama
english: "It would be hard for Kausalyā and Sumitrā, both tormented by grief for their sons, to survive with you as my mother."

sanskrit: nanu tv āryo 'pi dharmātmā tvayi vṛttim anuttamām vartate guruvṛttijño yathā mātari vartate
english: "Does not the noble and righteous Rāma, who knows how to conduct himself toward elders, treat you with the highest regard, as one would treat one's own mother?"

sanskrit: tathā jyeṣṭhā hi me mātā kausalyā dīrghadarśinī tvayi dharmaṃ samāsthāya bhaginyām iva vartate
english: "And Kausalyā, my eldest mother, far-sighted as she is, conducts herself toward you, upholding dharma, as toward a younger sister."

sanskrit: tasyāḥ putraṃ kṛtātmānaṃ cīravalkalavāsasaṃ prasthāpya vanavāsāya kathaṃ pāpe na śocasi
english: "Having sent her son — a man of perfected self, clad in bark-cloth garments — into forest exile, how do you not grieve, O sinful woman?"

sanskrit: apāpadarśinaṃ śūraṃ kṛtātmānaṃ yaśasvinam pravrājya cīravasanaṃ kiṃ nu paśyasi kāraṇam
english: "Having banished him who sees no evil in others, that hero, that self-perfected, glorious man, clad in bark — what reason do you see for it?"

sanskrit: lubdhāyā vidito manye na te 'haṃ rāghavaṃ prati tathā hy anartho rājyārthaṃ tvayā nīto mahān ayam
english: "I think you, greedy one, did not consider my regard for Rāghava; for this great calamity has been brought about by you for the sake of the kingdom."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi puruṣavyāghrāv apaśyan rāmalakṣmaṇau kena śaktiprabhāvena rājyaṃ rakṣitum utsahe
english: "Without seeing those two tigers among men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, by what power and prowess can I muster the will to protect this kingdom?"

sanskrit: taṃ hi nityaṃ mahārājo balavantaṃ mahābalaḥ apāśrito 'bhūd dharmātmā merur meruvanaṃ yathā
english: "The great king, mighty as he was, ever leaned on that powerful and righteous man, as Mount Meru leans upon the forests of Meru."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ katham imaṃ bhāraṃ mahādhuryasamudyatam damyo dhuram ivāsādya saheyaṃ kena caujasā
english: "How shall I, like a young ox put under a yoke fit for a great draught-animal, bear this burden by what strength?"

sanskrit: atha vā me bhavec chaktir yogair buddhibalena vā sakāmāṃ na kariṣyāmi tvām ahaṃ putragardhinīm nivartayiṣyāmi vanād bhrātaraṃ svajanapriyam
english: "Or if by discipline or by the strength of wisdom I find the power, I will not gratify you, you who are greedy for sons to rule — I shall bring back from the forest that brother who is dear to all our people."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā bharato mahātmā priyetarair vākyagaṇais tudaṃs tām śokāturaś cāpi nanāda bhūyaḥ siṃho yathā parvatagahvarasthaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the great-souled Bharata, tormenting her with these harsh words, and overcome with grief, roared once more like a lion lodged in a mountain cavern.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā garhayitvā tu mātaraṃ bharatas tadā roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭaḥ punar evābravīd vacaḥ
english: Having thus reproached his mother, Bharata, seized with great rage, spoke again:

sanskrit: rājyād bhraṃśasva kaikeyi nṛśaṃse duṣṭacāriṇi parityaktā ca dharmeṇa mā mṛtaṃ rudatī bhava
english: "Fall from the kingdom, Kaikeyī, O cruel and wicked woman! Cast off by righteousness, do not weep over the dead!"

sanskrit: kiṃ nu te 'dūṣayad rājā rāmo vā bhṛśadhārmikaḥ yayor mṛtyur vivāsaś ca tvatkṛte tulyam āgatau
english: "In what did the king wrong you, or Rāma, most steadfast in dharma — those two for whom, because of you, death and exile have alike arrived?"

sanskrit: bhrūṇahatyām asi prāptā kulasyāsya vināśanāt kaikeyi narakaṃ gaccha mā ca bhartuḥ salokatām
english: "You have incurred the guilt of brahminicide through the destruction of this lineage; go to hell, Kaikeyī — and do not share the world of your husband!"

sanskrit: yat tvayā hīdṛśaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ ghoreṇa karmaṇā sarvalokapriyaṃ hitvā mamāpy āpāditaṃ bhayam
english: "By this dreadful deed you have perpetrated such sin, abandoning him who is beloved of all the world, and have brought fear upon me as well."

sanskrit: tvatkṛte me pitā vṛtto rāmaś cāraṇyam āśritaḥ ayaśo jīvaloke ca tvayāhaṃ pratipāditaḥ
english: "Because of you my father has departed, and Rāma has taken refuge in the forest; and through you I have been endowed with infamy in the world of the living."

sanskrit: mātṛrūpe mamāmitre nṛśaṃse rājyakāmuke na te 'ham abhibhāṣyo 'smi durvṛtte patighātini
english: "You, who appear as a mother but are my enemy — you cruel, kingdom-hungry, wicked woman, murderess of your husband — I will not speak with you!"

sanskrit: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca yāś cānyā mama mātaraḥ duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭās tvāṃ prāpya kuladūṣiṇīm
english: "Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and all my other mothers are overwhelmed by great sorrow through you, the defiler of our lineage."

sanskrit: na tvam aśvapateḥ kanyā dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ rākṣasī tatra jātāsi kulapradhvaṃsinī pituḥ
english: "You are not the daughter of Aśvapati, the wise and righteous king — you are a rākṣasī born there, the destroyer of your father's lineage."

sanskrit: yat tvayā dhārmiko rāmo nityaṃ satyaparāyaṇaḥ vanaṃ prasthāpito duḥkhāt pitā ca tridivaṃ gataḥ
english: "Because you sent the righteous Rāma, ever devoted to truth, to the forest in sorrow, and my father has gone to the three worlds above —"

sanskrit: yat pradhānāsi tat pāpaṃ mayi pitrā vinākṛte bhrātṛbhyāṃ ca parityakte sarvalokasya cāpriye
english: "— the sin whose chief author you are falls on me, left without a father, abandoned by my brothers, and hateful in the eyes of all the world."

sanskrit: kausalyāṃ dharmasaṃyuktāṃ viyuktāṃ pāpaniścaye kṛtvā kaṃ prāpsyase tv adya lokaṃ nirayagāminī
english: "Having separated Kausalyā, who is united with dharma, from her son by your wicked resolve — what world will you attain today, O you who are destined for hell?"

sanskrit: kiṃ nāvabudhyase krūre niyataṃ bandhusaṃśrayam jyeṣṭhaṃ pitṛsamaṃ rāmaṃ kausalyāyātmasaṃbhavam
english: "Why, O cruel woman, do you not understand the certain bond of kinship with Rāma — the eldest, equal to a father — the very son born of Kausalyā?"

sanskrit: aṅgapratyaṅgajaḥ putro hṛdayāc cāpi jāyate tasmāt priyataro mātuḥ priyatvān na tu bāndhavaḥ
english: "A son is born from every limb and from the heart itself; therefore a son is dearer to a mother than even the dearest kinsman."

sanskrit: anyadā kila dharmajñā surabhiḥ surasaṃmatā vahamānau dadarśorvyāṃ putrau vigatacetasau
english: "It is told that once upon a time, Surabhī, the wish-granting cow, honored by the gods, goddess of dharma, saw her two sons utterly spent on the earth —"

sanskrit: tāv ardhadivase śrāntau dṛṣṭvā putrau mahītale ruroda putra śokena bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇā
english: "— seeing those two sons weary at midday on the ground, she wept with grief for her children, her eyes swimming with tears."

sanskrit: adhastād vrajatas tasyāḥ surarājño mahātmanaḥ bindavaḥ patitā gātre sūkṣmāḥ surabhigandhinaḥ
english: "Tiny fragrant drops fell from her onto the body of the great-souled king of gods who was passing below her."

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śokasaṃtaptāṃ vajrapāṇir yaśasvinīm indraḥ prāñjalir udvignaḥ surarājo 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: "Seeing her, the glorious one, scorched with grief, the wielder of the thunderbolt, Indra, king of gods, spoke with joined palms and in agitation:"

sanskrit: bhayaṃ kaccin na cāsmāsu kutaś cid vidyate mahat kuto nimittaḥ śokas te brūhi sarvahitaiṣiṇi
english: "'Is there perhaps some great fear from us or from anywhere? What is the cause of your grief? Tell me, O you who wish the welfare of all.'"

sanskrit: evam uktā tu surabhiḥ surarājena dhīmatā patyuvāca tato dhīrā vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradā
english: Thus addressed by the wise king of gods, the steady Surabhī, skilled in speech, spoke to her lord:

sanskrit: śāntaṃ pātaṃ na vaḥ kiṃ cit kutaś cid amarādhipa ahaṃ tu magnau śocāmi svaputrau viṣame sthitau
english: "'May what is auspicious befall you — there is no danger from you or from anywhere, O lord of immortals; but I grieve for my two sons sunk in hardship.'"

sanskrit: etau dṛṣṭvā kṛśau dīnau sūryaraśmipratāpinau vadhyamānau balīvardau karṣakeṇa surādhipa
english: "'Seeing these two lean and pitiful bullocks, scorched by the sun's rays, being beaten by a ploughman, O lord of gods —'"

sanskrit: mama kāyāt prasūtau hi duḥkhitau bhāra pīḍitau yau dṛṣṭvā paritapye 'haṃ nāsti putrasamaḥ priyaḥ
english: "'— these two born from my own body, pained and crushed by their burden — seeing them I am afflicted. There is nothing as dear as a son.'"

sanskrit: yasyāḥ putra sahasrāṇi sāpi śocati kāmadhuk kiṃ punar yā vinā rāmaṃ kausalyā vartayiṣyati
english: "If even Surabhī, the wish-fulfilling cow who has thousands of sons, grieves thus, how then shall Kausalyā, bereft of Rāma, bear to go on?"

sanskrit: ekaputrā ca sādhvī ca vivatseyaṃ tvayā kṛtā tasmāt tvaṃ satataṃ duḥkhaṃ pretya ceha ca lapsyase
english: "She is virtuous, has but a single son, and you have made her bereft as a cow that has lost its calf; therefore you shall suffer constantly, both in this world and the next."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hy apacitiṃ bhrātuḥ pituś ca sakalām imām vardhanaṃ yaśasaś cāpi kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ
english: "I myself will fully honor the debt to my brother and to my father, and I will increase their glory — of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: ānāyayitvā tanayaṃ kausalyāyā mahādyutim svayam eva pravekṣyāmi vanaṃ muniniṣevitam
english: "Having brought back the exceedingly radiant son of Kausalyā, I myself will enter the forest frequented by sages."

sanskrit: iti nāga ivāraṇye tomarāṅkuśacoditaḥ papāta bhuvi saṃkruddho niḥśvasann iva pannagaḥ
english: Thus speaking, he fell to the ground in furious rage like an elephant in the forest driven by goad and lance, hissing like a serpent.

sanskrit: saṃraktanetraḥ śithilāmbaras tadā vidhūtasarvābharaṇaḥ paraṃtapaḥ babhūva bhūmau patito nṛpātmajaḥ śacīpateḥ ketur ivotsavakṣaye
english: With reddened eyes, his garments loose, all his ornaments shaken off, that scorcher of enemies, the son of the king, lay fallen on the ground like the banner of Śacī's lord at the close of a festival.

sanskrit: tathaiva krośatas tasya bharatasya mahātmanaḥ kausalyā śabdam ājñāya sumitrām idam abravīt
english: Even as the great-souled Bharata was crying out in that manner, Kausalyā, recognizing his voice, said this to Sumitrā:

sanskrit: āgataḥ krūrakāryāyāḥ kaikeyyā bharataḥ sutaḥ tam ahaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi bharataṃ dīrghadarśinam
english: "Bharata, the son of cruel-deeded Kaikeyī, has come; I wish to see that far-sighted Bharata."

sanskrit: evam uktvā sumitrāṃ sā vivarṇā malināmbarā pratasthe bharato yatra vepamānā vicetanā
english: Having spoken thus to Sumitrā, she — pale, wearing soiled garments, trembling and all but senseless — made her way to where Bharata was.

sanskrit: sa tu rāmānujaś cāpi śatrughnasahitas tadā pratasthe bharato yatra kausalyāyā niveśanam
english: And Bharata, that younger brother of Rāma, accompanied by Śatrughna, then made his way to Kausalyā's dwelling.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatrughnabharatau kausalyāṃ prekṣya duḥkhitau paryaṣvajetāṃ duḥkhārtāṃ patitāṃ naṣṭacetanām
english: Then Śatrughna and Bharata, seeing Kausalyā afflicted with grief, embraced her — stricken with sorrow, fallen to the ground, her senses gone.

sanskrit: bharataṃ pratyuvācedaṃ kausalyā bhṛśaduḥkhitā idaṃ te rājyakāmasya rājyaṃ prāptam akaṇṭakam saṃprāptaṃ bata kaikeyyā śīghraṃ krūreṇa karmaṇā
english: Kausalyā, deeply grief-stricken, addressed Bharata: "This uncontested kingdom desired by you has been obtained — alas, gained swiftly by Kaikeyī through a cruel deed."

sanskrit: prasthāpya cīravasanaṃ putraṃ me vanavāsinam kaikeyī kaṃ guṇaṃ tatra paśyati krūradarśinī
english: "Having sent my son clad in bark-cloth to dwell in the forest, what virtue does cruel-sighted Kaikeyī see in it?"

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ mām api kaikeyī prasthāpayitum arhati hiraṇyanābho yatrāste suto me sumahāyaśāḥ
english: "Kaikeyī should quickly send me away as well, to wherever my son of surpassing glory, Hiraṇyanābha, dwells."

sanskrit: atha vā svayam evāhaṃ sumitrānucarā sukham agnihotraṃ puraskṛtya prasthāsye yatra rāghavaḥ
english: "Or else I myself, with Sumitrā accompanying me, will gladly set out, placing the agnihotra fire before me, to wherever Rāghava is."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ vā svayam evādya tatra māṃ netum arhasi yatrāsau puruṣavyāghras tapyate me tapaḥ sutaḥ
english: "Or if you wish, you yourself should lead me there today, to where that tiger among men, my son, performs his austerities."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi tava vistīrṇaṃ dhanadhānyasamācitam hastyaśvarathasaṃpūrṇaṃ rājyaṃ niryātitaṃ tayā
english: "This vast kingdom, filled with wealth and grain, full of elephants, horses, and chariots — this has been handed over to you by her."

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapamānāṃ tāṃ bharataḥ prāñjalis tadā kausalyāṃ pratyuvācedaṃ śokair bahubhir āvṛtām
english: Then Bharata, with joined palms, addressed Kausalyā thus as she lamented, overwhelmed by many sorrows:

sanskrit: ārye kasmād ajānantaṃ garhase mām akilbiṣam vipulāṃ ca mama prītiṃ sthirāṃ jānāsi rāghave
english: "Revered one, why do you reproach me, innocent as I am and knowing nothing? You know my great and steadfast love for Rāghava."

sanskrit: kṛtā śāstrānugā buddhir mā bhūt tasya kadā cana satyasaṃdhaḥ satāṃ śreṣṭho yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "May there never arise in him whose sanction the noble one departed — that truest of the faithful, best among the righteous — a thought contrary to the scriptures."

sanskrit: praiṣyaṃ pāpīyasāṃ yātu sūryaṃ ca prati mehatu hantu pādena gāṃ suptāṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "Let him in whose consent the noble one went become a slave of the wicked, make water toward the sun, and kick a sleeping cow with his foot."

sanskrit: kārayitvā mahat karma bhartā bhṛtyam anarthakam adharmo yo 'sya so 'syās tu yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "Whatever sin falls on a master who assigns a great and useless task to a servant — let that same sin fall on him in whose sanction the noble one departed."

sanskrit: paripālayamānasya rājño bhūtāni putravat tatas tu druhyatāṃ pāpaṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "The sin of those who betray a king who protects his people like his own children — let that sin fall on him in whose sanction the noble one departed."

sanskrit: baliṣaḍbhāgam uddhṛtya nṛpasyārakṣataḥ prajāḥ adharmo yo 'sya so 'syāstu yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "The sin of a king who extracts the sixth part of the harvest as tribute but does not protect his subjects — let that sin fall on him in whose sanction the noble one departed."

sanskrit: saṃśrutya ca tapasvibhyaḥ satre vai yajñadakṣiṇām tāṃ vipralapatāṃ pāpaṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "The sin of those who promise sacrificial fees to ascetics at a soma sacrifice and then go back on their word — let that sin fall on him in whose sanction the noble one departed."

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathasaṃbādhe yuddhe śastrasamākule mā sma kārṣīt satāṃ dharmaṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "May he in whose sanction the noble one departed never observe the dharma of the righteous in the midst of battle, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, and bristling with weapons."

sanskrit: upadiṣṭaṃ susūkṣmārthaṃ śāstraṃ yatnena dhīmatā sa nāśayatu duṣṭātmā yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "Let that wicked-souled one in whose sanction the noble one departed destroy the scripture of subtle meaning carefully taught by a wise man."

sanskrit: pāyasaṃ kṛsaraṃ chāgaṃ vṛthā so 'śnātu nirghṛṇaḥ gurūṃś cāpy avajānātu yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "Let that merciless one in whose sanction the noble one departed eat rice-pudding, porridge, and goat-flesh uselessly, and disrespect his elders as well."

sanskrit: putrair dāraiś ca bhṛtyaiś ca svagṛhe parivāritaḥ sa eko mṛṣṭam aśnātu yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "Let him in whose sanction the noble one departed eat choice food alone, even while surrounded in his own house by his sons, wives, and servants."

sanskrit: rājastrībālavṛddhānāṃ vadhe yat pāpam ucyate bhṛtyatyāge ca yat pāpaṃ tat pāpaṃ pratipadyatām
english: "Let them incur the sin declared for the killing of royal women, children, and the elderly, and the sin for the abandonment of one's servants."

sanskrit: ubhe saṃdhye śayānasya yat pāpaṃ parikalpyate tac ca pāpaṃ bhavet tasya yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "The sin reckoned for one who sleeps through both twilight junctures — let that sin also befall him in whose sanction the noble one departed."

sanskrit: yad agnidāyake pāpaṃ yat pāpaṃ gurutalpage mitradrohe ca yat pāpaṃ tat pāpaṃ pratipadyatām
english: "Whatever sin falls on one who sets fire to another's house, whatever sin on one who strikes his elder, and whatever sin on one who betrays a friend — let them incur all those sins."

sanskrit: devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca mātā pitros tathaiva ca mā sma kārṣīt sa śuśrūṣāṃ yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "May he in whose sanction the noble one departed never render service to the gods, to the ancestors, or to his own mother and father."

sanskrit: satāṃ lokāt satāṃ kīrtyāḥ sajjuṣṭāt karmaṇas tathā bhraśyatu kṣipram adyaiva yasyāryo 'numate gataḥ
english: "Let him in whose sanction the noble one departed fall immediately this very day from the world of the righteous, from the fame of the righteous, and from deeds held dear by the righteous."

sanskrit: vihīnāṃ patiputrābhyāṃ kausalyāṃ pārthivātmajaḥ evam āśvasayann eva duḥkhārto nipapāta ha
english: Even as he spoke thus to console Kausalyā — bereft of both husband and son — the king's son, overcome with grief, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tathā tu śapathaiḥ kaṣṭais śapamānam acetanam bharataṃ śokasaṃtaptaṃ kausalyā vākyam abravīt
english: Then Kausalyā spoke to Bharata, who was swearing those terrible oaths, senseless and scorched with sorrow:

sanskrit: mama duḥkham idaṃ putra bhūyaḥ samupajāyate śapathaiḥ śapamāno hi prāṇān uparuṇatsi me
english: "My grief, my son, is multiplied anew; for as you swear these oaths, you choke the very life out of me."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā na calito dharmād ātmā te sahalakṣmaṇaḥ vatsa satyapratijño me satāṃ lokān avāpsyasi
english: "By good fortune your soul, together with Lakṣmaṇa's, has not swerved from dharma; my dear child, true to your vow, you shall attain the worlds of the righteous."

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapamānasya duḥkhārtasya mahātmanaḥ mohāc ca śokasaṃrodhād babhūva lulitaṃ manaḥ
english: Thus lamenting, the great-souled one, afflicted with grief, his mind disordered from both stupor and the onslaught of sorrow, was utterly broken.

sanskrit: lālapyamānasya vicetanasya pranaṣṭabuddheḥ patitasya bhūmau muhur muhur niḥśvasataś ca dīrghaṃ sā tasya śokena jagāma rātriḥ
english: For him — delirious, senseless, his reason lost, fallen on the ground, heaving long sighs again and again — that night passed in grief.
